# DOAS: Double Observer Adjusted Survey

The **DOAS** R package provides a unified Frequentist and Hierarchical
Bayesian statistical framework to estimate wildlife population abundance
from either **full Double Observer (DO) surveys** (100% of sectors
surveyed by two observers) or **partial Double Observer Adjusted Surveys
(DOAS)** that combine targeted DO surveys in a subset of sectors with
single-observer block counts across the remaining study area.

By calibrating detection probability on the Double Observer sectors—and
optionally modeling both detection covariates (`p_formula`) and
habitat/abundance covariates (`n_formula`)—`DOAS` corrects for imperfect
detection ($`p < 1`$) across entire landscapes while substantially
reducing field personnel requirements.

## Installation

You can install the development version of `DOAS` from GitHub using
`devtools`:

``` r

# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("achazhardenberg/DOAS", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

## Overview of Features

### 1. Flexible Data Ingestion & Validation

- **[`doas_data()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/doas_data.md)**:
  Validates and standardizes survey data from three field recording
  formats into a `doas_data` object (with a dedicated
  [`print()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/print.html) summary):
  - `format = "sector"`: Wide sector-level summaries (`total_count`,
    `detected_groups`, `groups_both`, `groups_obs1`, `groups_obs2`).
    Automatically infers `detected_groups` or `groups_both` if one is
    omitted in DO sectors, retains all sector-level covariate columns,
    and flags sectors with `total_count = NA` as `"Unsurveyed"` for
    prediction via `n_formula`.
  - `format = "group"`: Long group-level capture histories (one row per
    detected animal group with `obs1` and `obs2` binary detection
    indicators).
  - `format = "sighting"`: Long observer-sighting records reconciled by
    `group_id` and `observer`.

### 2. Frequentist & Hierarchical Bayesian Abundance Estimators

- **[`doas()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/doas.md)**:
  Core abundance estimator supporting both full Double Observer surveys
  and partial DOAS designs via orthogonal arguments:
  - **`method = c("frequentist", "bayesian")`**: Choose between
    Frequentist estimation (with analytical multivariate Delta-method or
    non-parametric spatial block `"bootstrap"` confidence intervals) and
    pure-R multi-chain Hierarchical Bayesian MCMC estimation (reporting
    posterior means, 95% credible intervals, Gelman–Rubin $`\hat{R}`$,
    and effective sample size $`n_{\text{eff}}`$).
  - **`obs_type = c("independent", "dependent")`**: Supports both
    simultaneous independent observers (Chapman mark–recapture with
    symmetric observer pool efficiency $`\bar{p} = (p_1 + p_2)/2`$) and
    dependent primary–secondary observer protocols (Zippin removal).
  - **`pooling = c("hybrid", "global")`**: `"hybrid"` (default) retains
    direct mark–recapture estimates inside surveyed DO sectors and
    extrapolates only single-observer Block sectors; `"global"` applies
    the calibrated single-observer detection rate across all surveyed
    sectors.
  - **`p_formula = ~ ...`**: Models sector-level variation in detection
    probability using standard R linear model formulas (supporting
    multiple covariates, interaction terms such as
    `~ effort * ruggedness`, and polynomial terms).
  - **`n_formula = ~ ...`**: Models sector-level abundance
    ($`\log \lambda_i = \mathbf{z}_i^\top \boldsymbol{\gamma}`$) as a
    function of environmental covariates (e.g.,
    `~ elevation + habitat + offset(log(area))`), automatically imputing
    any unsurveyed sectors (`total_count = NA`).
- **[`predict.doas()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/predict.doas.md)**:
  S3 [`predict()`](https://rdrr.io/r/stats/predict.html) method that
  predicts sector abundance (`type = "abundance"`), group count
  (`type = "groups"`), or detection probability (`type = "detection"`)
  with standard errors and 95% confidence/credible intervals for
  in-sample sectors or new covariate grids (`newdata`).
- **Low-Level Building Blocks**:
  - [`chapman_estimate()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/chapman_estimate.md)
    &
    [`chapman_variance()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/chapman_variance.md):
    Bias-corrected independent double-observer estimator and
    Seber (1982) variance.
  - [`dependent_zippin_estimate()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/dependent_zippin_estimate.md)
    &
    [`dependent_zippin_variance()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/dependent_zippin_variance.md):
    Primary–secondary observer removal estimator and variance.
  - [`bayesian_conjugate_estimate()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/bayesian_conjugate_estimate.md):
    Bound-safe multi-chain conjugate Beta–Binomial MCMC abundance
    estimator for DO sectors.

### 3. Information-Theoretic Model Selection

- **[`QAIC()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/QAIC.md)**:
  Computes the Quasi-Akaike Information Criterion ($`\hat{c}`$, $`K`$,
  $`\Delta\text{QAIC}`$) to rank competing frequentist `doas` detection
  (`p_formula`) or abundance (`n_formula`) models while accounting for
  overdispersion.
- **[`WAIC()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/WAIC.md)**:
  Computes the Widely Applicable Information Criterion ($`\text{lppd}`$,
  $`p_{\text{WAIC}}`$, $`\Delta\text{WAIC}`$) from the pointwise
  posterior log-likelihood matrix of Bayesian `doas` models.

### 4. Simulation & Prospective Power Analysis

- **[`simulate_pop()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/simulate_pop.md)**:
  Generates spatially structured animal populations partitioned into
  groups across sectors.
- **[`simulate_survey()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/simulate_survey.md)**:
  Simulates full DO or partial DOAS surveys with group-size scaling,
  counting error, inter-observer skill differences (`obs_effect`),
  inter-sector heterogeneity (`detvar`), and sector covariate effects
  (`cov_effect`).
- **[`doas_power()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/doas_power.md)**:
  Conducts Monte Carlo power and accuracy analyses across varying
  numbers of Double Observer sectors (`surv_areas`) for any combination
  of `method`, `obs_type`, `pooling`, `p_formula`, and `n_formula`.

## Quick Start Example

``` r

library(DOAS)

# 1. Simulate a 24-sector population (~3500 animals) with a habitat effect on abundance,
#    and a partial DOAS survey (12 DO sectors, 12 Block sectors) with an effort effect on detection
set.seed(12)
pop <- simulate_pop(
  pop_size   = 3500,
  mean_group = 8,
  tot_areas  = 24,
  n_formula  = ~ habitat,
  n_betas    = c(habitat = 0.5)
)
raw_data <- simulate_survey(
  sim_pop         = pop,
  det_p1          = 0.55,
  intra_group_det = 1.0,
  det_group       = 0.95,
  obs_effect      = 0.90,
  detvar          = 0.02,
  surv_areas      = 12,
  p_formula       = ~ effort,
  p_betas         = c(effort = 1.0)
)

survey_dat <- doas_data(raw_data, format = "sector")
print(head(survey_dat))

# 2. Maximum Likelihood (ML) Estimation (Detection & Abundance Covariates)
fit_ml_cov <- doas(
  survey_dat,
  method    = "ML",
  obs_type  = "independent",
  pooling   = "hybrid",
  p_formula = ~ effort,
  n_formula = ~ habitat
)

fit_ml_null <- doas(
  survey_dat,
  method    = "ML",
  obs_type  = "independent",
  pooling   = "hybrid",
  p_formula = ~ 1,
  n_formula = ~ habitat
)

summary(fit_ml_cov)
cat("True simulated population:", pop$tot_pop, "\n")
QAIC(fit_ml_cov, fit_ml_null)

# Predict detection probability and expected abundance across a covariate gradient
new_sectors <- data.frame(effort = c(-1, 0, 1), habitat = c(-1, 0, 1))
predict(fit_ml_cov, newdata = new_sectors, type = "detection")
predict(fit_ml_cov, newdata = new_sectors, type = "abundance")

# 3. Multi-Chain Hierarchical Bayesian Estimation & WAIC Selection
fit_bayes_null <- doas(
  survey_dat,
  method   = "Bayes",
  obs_type = "independent",
  pooling  = "hybrid",
  chains   = 3,
  iter     = 2000,
  burnin   = 500
)

fit_bayes_cov <- doas(
  survey_dat,
  method    = "Bayes",
  obs_type  = "independent",
  pooling   = "hybrid",
  p_formula = ~ effort,
  n_formula = ~ habitat,
  chains    = 3,
  iter      = 2000,
  burnin    = 500
)

summary(fit_bayes_cov)
WAIC(fit_bayes_null, fit_bayes_cov)
```

## Documentation & Tutorials

A step-by-step tutorial vignette covering field data preparation,
frequentist and Bayesian estimation, covariate selection, and
prospective power analysis is included with the package:

``` r

vignette("DOAS-tutorial", package = "DOAS")
```

## Citation & Methods

If you use `DOAS` in your research, please cite both the R package and
the original methodological paper introducing the Double Observer
Adjusted Survey framework:

> von Hardenberg, A. (2026). *DOAS: Double Observer Adjusted Survey
> Framework*. R package version 1.0.0.
> <https://github.com/achazhardenberg/DOAS>
>
> Panaccio, M., Brambilla, A., Bassano, B., Smith, T., & von Hardenberg,
> A. (2024). A new double observer-based census framework to improve
> abundance estimations in mountain ungulates and other gregarious
> species with a reduced effort. *Ecological Solutions and Evidence*,
> 5(4), e12405. <https://doi.org/10.1002/2688-8319.12405>

# Package index

## Main Estimation Workflow

Top-level functions to structure field data and estimate abundance.

- [`doas()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/doas.md)
  [`summary(`*`<doas>`*`)`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/doas.md)
  : Double Observer Adjusted Survey (DOAS) Abundance Estimation
- [`doas_data()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/doas_data.md)
  : Format and Validate Survey Data for DOAS
- [`predict(`*`<doas>`*`)`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/predict.doas.md)
  : Predict Method for DOAS Models
- [`print(`*`<doas_data>`*`)`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/print.doas_data.md)
  : Print Method for Validated DOAS Survey Data

## Simulation & Power Analysis

Tools to simulate cluster-sampled populations, survey protocols, and run
power analyses.

- [`simulate_pop()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/simulate_pop.md)
  : Simulate a Population
- [`simulate_survey()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/simulate_survey.md)
  : Simulate a Survey and format for DOAS
- [`doas_power()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/doas_power.md)
  : DOAS Power Analysis

## Model Selection

Information criteria for frequentist and Bayesian models.

- [`QAIC()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/QAIC.md) :
  Quasi-Akaike Information Criterion (QAIC)
- [`WAIC()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/WAIC.md) :
  Widely Applicable Information Criterion (WAIC)

## Base Estimators

Underlying mathematical estimators for mark-recapture and removal
setups.

- [`chapman_estimate()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/chapman_estimate.md)
  : Calculate Chapman-adjusted Lincoln-Petersen estimate
- [`chapman_variance()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/chapman_variance.md)
  : Calculate Variance of the Chapman estimator
- [`dependent_zippin_estimate()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/dependent_zippin_estimate.md)
  : Calculate Dependent Double Observer (Zippin) Estimate
- [`dependent_zippin_variance()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/dependent_zippin_variance.md)
  : Calculate Variance of the Dependent Double Observer (Zippin)
  estimator
- [`bayesian_conjugate_estimate()`](https://achazhardenberg.github.io/DOAS/reference/bayesian_conjugate_estimate.md)
  : Calculate Bayesian Multi-Chain MCMC Double Observer Estimate
